Alex / Sofia — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Key pain points (what you told us):
- Unit economics for inference are the top constraint: your per-conversation cost has increased ~2.5x over the last 6 months as model sizes and QPS have grown.
- Current stack: self-hosted mix of open models on k8s + some vendor API fallbacks for spikes; inference ops are a heavy maintenance burden.
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 800ms for user-facing flows; batch workloads can tolerate higher latency.
- Accuracy sensitivity: you can tolerate small downstream metric drift, but not >5% drop in NLU intents.

Success criteria (what success looks like to you):
- 2-3x reduction in $/inference (unit cost) without noticeable drop in user metrics
- Maintain P95 <= 800ms for interactive routes
- Clear migration path with canary rollout and automatic fallback to current infra

Technical openness / constraints you shared:
- Open to quantization (4-bit preferred if accuracy holds), but need validation on your eval set
- Want smarter batching/caching: optimistic expectation is 20-40% unit-cost reduction from batching+prefix caching
- Security: SOC2 + ability to run in your VPC for production workloads

Proposed next steps (agreed on call):
1) Ben and I will schedule a 60-min technical deep dive next week to look at your traffic profile, sequence-length distribution, and a sample eval set.
2) We’ll provide a preliminary MAP (mutual action plan) and a solution overview deck (attached) by EOD Friday.
3) Run a small pilot: 1-2 models, ~10% traffic, measure unit economics and intent metrics over 2 weeks.

Action items:
- Marissa: share MAP + solution deck (attached) — EOD Fri (11/20)
- Ben: prepare scope for technical call and list of telemetry we need (QPS, avg/95 seq length, token mix)
- Alex: confirm 30-60 minute slots for technical deep dive next week and share a representative eval set (or access)

Attachments: Redwood_Solution_Overview.pdf (overview + quantization profiles)

Thanks — happy to iterate on this. If I missed anything or misstated a priority, call it out and I’ll update.

Best,

Alex / Marissa — quick technical note ahead of our deep dive:

Summary of what Redwood can validate quickly and what we’ll need from you:
- Caching: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching at the serving layer; for sessioned conversational flows we commonly see 20-35% token reduction (and corresponding cost) once caching is enabled for repeated prefixes. Yes — stateful per-user session caching is supported.
- Batching: our runtime optimizes for continuous batching with adaptive batch sizing; for interactive routes we typically see effective batch sizes of 6-12 depending on arrival patterns.
- Quantization: we have validated 4-bit and 8-bit variants for many open models. For sensitive NLU flows we recommend an A/B evaluation on your intent/slot eval set — if metrics hold within your tolerance we can proceed to pilot.
- Telemetry we need for initial sizing: avg QPS by route, P50/P95 latency by route, seq length distribution histogram (bins: 0-64,65-128,129-256,256+), and sample eval dataset and labels.

Pilot template (what I’ll propose on call):
1) Small pilot: 1 model, 10% production traffic for 2 weeks; collect unit-cost delta, latency, and intent metrics.
2) If pilot meets guardrails (<=5% intent drift, P95 target met, >=2x unit-cost improvement target partially met), scale to 50% with canary and auto-fallback.

I’ve attached a short MAP template and a checklist of required telemetry for the call. Looking forward to the deep dive — I’ll bring runtime perf numbers for the model families you mentioned.

Cheers,
